stories.normalized_subject: nvidia reportedly asks global cloud partners to keep 51% of services outside china
stories.event_summary: The Financial Times reports that Nvidia has told data-centre partners worldwide to direct at least 51% of their cloud services to customers outside China. The instruction was reportedly delivered verbally by sales and regional teams, applies to future contracts and leaves existing leases untouched. The FT cites five people familiar with the policy; it has not published a written Nvidia rule. Nvidia’s public response defended the role of US-built data centres and said longstanding US policy encourages American infrastructure to win business worldwide. That statement did not confirm the reported 51% requirement. If enforced, the rule could make overseas GPU leasing harder for Chinese model developers and change the economics of cloud operators in Southeast Asia and other regional hubs.
stories.normalized_headline: Nvidia reportedly asks global cloud partners to keep 51% of services outside China
stories.delivery_note: This is an FT-reported policy, not a confirmed public Nvidia rule or a US government regulation. The 51% figure and scope should be treated as reported, not independently documented.

stories.normalized_subject: indiaai mission releases eka-1 and two dhīr models for local and offline deployment

The government describes Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B as open-source multilingual assistants for English and 10 Indian languages, with offline-capable, on-premises use for document-grounded automation and knowledge retrieval. The teams received subsidised national AI compute and research support. The release is evidence of a domestic model pipeline, but not yet proof of competitive benchmarks, sustained adoption or production-grade support.

stories.normalized_subject: drax and brookfield outline a uk ai campus with more than 1gw of potential capacity
stories.event_summary: Drax, Brookfield and its AI infrastructure platform Radiant signed a partnership to develop data-centre capacity at Drax Power Station in North Yorkshire. The partners are targeting more than 1GW across several phases. Phase one is up to 100MW, with commercial operations targeted for the first quarter of 2028; a later phase could add 500MW between 2028 and 2031. Brookfield estimates the full development could attract more than £20bn, including about £2.5bn for the first phase. Drax says the site has about 4GW of grid access and 2.6GW of active dispatchable generation. Phase one is expected to draw power directly from the grid; later phases may use a behind-the-meter arrangement. Planning, network and regulatory approvals, a suitable tenant, commercial agreements and final investment decisions are still required.

stories.normalized_subject: crowdstrike is buying agent observability and ai red-team tools — and adding a kill switch
stories.event_summary: CrowdStrike signed agreements to acquire Fiddler AI, which monitors and explains agent behaviour, and Dreadnode, which tests models and agents for security weaknesses. The Wall Street Journal reports a combined price of $495m, mostly cash; CrowdStrike’s official announcements do not disclose the purchase price. Fiddler is intended to add pre-deployment evaluation, traceability of decisions and tool calls, and production monitoring. CrowdStrike says it plans to support OpenTelemetry and frameworks including LangGraph, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Strands and Google ADK. Dreadnode is designed to run more than 100 attack strategies, including jailbreaks, prompt injection and multi-turn agent attacks, against models, applications and MCP servers. Separately, CrowdStrike announced an AI kill switch and an AI Gateway in Falcon Guardian. The gateway is available now; endpoint termination is described as coming later. Acquired Fiddler and Dreadnode capabilities are planned for general availability in Q4 FY27, subject to closing and integration.

stories.normalized_subject: meta raises $15bn in bonds as ai infrastructure spending moves deeper into debt markets
stories.event_summary: Meta is raising $15bn through a five-part US-dollar bond offering, according to Reuters and a regulatory filing. The company expects 2026 capital expenditure of $135bn to $145bn, largely tied to AI infrastructure. It previously raised $25bn in April and $30bn last year. Meta’s total debt stood at $83.67bn at the end of September, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters. The sale is a financing decision, not proof that Meta has exhausted its cash or that the entire amount is earmarked for a single AI project. It shows how quickly compute ambitions are becoming a capital-markets story: data centres, power, networking and accelerators must be funded years before all the capacity earns a return.

stories.normalized_subject: google’s school ai opt-in comes with a search trade-off
stories.event_summary: Google says Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be off for K–12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly enable them. Guided Learning is now globally available in Google Classroom, and Google is building step-by-step tutoring into Search, with a pilot in selected US schools later in November. There is a catch for districts that want AI disabled: Google says Search and AI are deeply integrated, so turning the products off also removes Search access for student accounts. Google frames the change as giving schools control. Educators and public officials quoted by AP and other outlets argue that the coupling pressures schools to accept AI to retain a basic search tool.

stories.normalized_subject: apple’s margin warning shows the ai memory crunch reaching consumer devices

Reuters reports that Apple is forecasting a 45%–46% gross margin for the December quarter and has increased manufacturing purchase obligations by $33bn to $89.7bn. Apple has been drawing on memory bought earlier at lower prices while securing additional supply. Reuters links the squeeze to AI data-centre demand absorbing memory capacity. stories.normalized_subject: former openai staff say they warned leaders about internal security gaps for years

The concerns predated ChatGPT’s launch, according to the report. OpenAI told Reuters that its most sensitive work is held separately with strict access controls, that the monorepo does not contain all of its code or model weights, and that it now conducts regular security reviews of internal tools. The reporting describes employee warnings and security-process concerns; it does not establish that every alleged weakness led to a breach.

stories.event_summary: AI satellite maker Adaspace raised HK$750m in its Hong Kong IPO and fell 1.2% on its first trading day.
stories.normalized_headline: AI satellite maker Adaspace slips 1.2% on its Hong Kong debut
stories.delivery_note: IPO proceeds and first-day share movement are reported market facts; the company’s satellite AI capabilities remain company-described.

stories.normalized_subject: US AI task force discussion of AI-powered cyberattack reporting
stories.event_summary: The White House AI task force discussed reporting standards and information sharing for AI-powered cyberattacks as the 2015 Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act approaches expiry.
stories.normalized_headline: Trump’s AI task force discusses reporting AI-powered cyberattacks
stories.delivery_note: The meeting produced discussion, not a new rule or formal decision.

stories.normalized_subject: AI companies recruit former intelligence and counterintelligence staff
stories.event_summary: Reuters reports frontier AI companies are hiring counterintelligence specialists to protect model weights, code and trade secrets, with some job postings offering $200,000–$500,000 salaries.
stories.normalized_headline: AI firms are recruiting former intelligence officers to protect trade secrets
stories.delivery_note: Hiring trend is based on Reuters reporting and job postings; advertised compensation is not a uniform salary range.

stories.normalized_subject: AMD expands Instinct MI400 with MI450X, new MI455X inference results and MI430X scientific-computing details
stories.event_summary: On 12 November 2026 AMD expanded its Instinct MI400 portfolio with the MI450X GPU, offering 288GB of HBM4 per GPU while retaining the MI455X compute, bandwidth and connectivity profile. AMD also published a vendor-run MI455X/Helios DeepSeek-R1 result of 21,333 tokens per second per GPU in an MLPerf Inference Offline configuration, which AMD says is up to 30% above Nvidia Vera Rubin's latest published result. AMD added MI430X scientific-computing specifications: up to 288 TFLOPs FP64, 432GB HBM4 and up to 23.3TB/s bandwidth; availability is expected in 2027. The benchmark comparison is not an independent identical-system test; product availability and real workloads remain to be established.
stories.normalized_headline: AMD adds a 288GB HBM4 MI450X and publishes new Helios inference numbers
source_metadata: AMD Instinct MI430X product information · accessed 13 Nov 2026
stories.delivery_note: Material follow-up to AMD's 3 November Q3/Helios story. MI455X throughput and bandwidth comparisons are vendor-run or vendor-calculated; no independent identical-system comparison was published in this source set.
stories.material_change: Adds a new MI450X 288GB HBM4 configuration, MI430X scientific-computing specifications and a new AMD-run MI455X DeepSeek-R1 inference result. This is more than a fresh article about the prior Q3 results.

stories.normalized_subject: Nebius Q3 2026 results, third-party data-centre capacity delays and revised revenue/capex guidance
stories.event_summary: Nebius reported Q3 2026 revenue of US$981m, above the US$907.5m estimate cited by Reuters, and lowered its 2026 revenue range to US$3.0–3.2bn after some third-party data-centre capacity expected in 2026 moved to H1 2027. The company says the contracts remain in place and its own sites are on schedule or ahead. It raised 2026 capex guidance to about US$27bn and expects US$40–45bn in 2027, with 75–85% of next year's spending expected to be covered by customer prepayments and asset-backed financing. Nebius forecasts US$12–13bn 2027 revenue and pre-tax break-even by year-end. Reuters reports a 16% share-price fall; this is an execution and financing signal, not proof of a broad demand collapse.
stories.normalized_headline: Nebius cuts its 2026 revenue range after third-party data-centre capacity slips
stories.delivery_note: Nebius says delayed third-party capacity remains contracted and its own sites are on schedule. The revised revenue outlook and capex are company guidance; the share-price move is Reuters reporting.

stories.normalized_subject: LMSYS launches a cross-vendor SGLang consortium to coordinate open inference roadmap work
stories.event_summary: On 12 November 2026 LMSYS Org launched the SGLang Consortium with Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Google, Meta, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk as founding members. The group will coordinate work on frontier-model support, reasoning and multimodal workloads, distributed inference and hardware optimization. Members appoint technical representatives and hold two roadmap meetings per year; working groups can collaborate between meetings. LMSYS maintainers retain technical decision-making and code-acceptance authority and the project remains open to the wider community. LMSYS says SGLang runs on hundreds of thousands of GPUs; that scale figure is a project claim, and the announcement includes no new independent benchmark.
stories.normalized_headline: Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Google and Meta join a new SGLang inference consortium
stories.delivery_note: The consortium is a roadmap forum, not a closed fork. The project's deployment-scale figures are attributed to LMSYS.

stories.normalized_subject: OpenAI enables limited GPT-6 Luna API regional processing and storage in India
stories.event_summary: OpenAI added India as a regional-processing location for eligible API customers on 12 November 2026. Supported GPT-6 Luna requests can be processed and stored in India through the Responses and Chat Completions APIs using an India project and in.api.openai.com. OpenAI's developer documentation specifies active Zero Data Retention (ZDR), Standard pay-as-you-go, and no hosted tools for regional processing in India. This does not apply to the consumer ChatGPT app or every model and workflow; customers must review their full data path and eligibility.
stories.normalized_headline: OpenAI adds in-country API processing for eligible Indian customers
stories.delivery_note: Official documentation specifies active ZDR, Standard pay-as-you-go, supported GPT-6 Luna endpoints and no hosted tools. This is not a general data-localisation or regulatory-compliance certification.

stories.normalized_subject: AMD plans equity investment and expanded quantum/HPC/AI infrastructure partnership with PsiQuantum
stories.event_summary: On 12 November 2026 AMD and PsiQuantum announced an expanded strategic partnership to co-design infrastructure for utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers and develop hybrid applications combining quantum, high-performance and AI computing. AMD brings Versal FPGAs, Instinct GPUs, EPYC CPUs and ROCm; PsiQuantum contributes its silicon-photonics platform. AMD plans an equity investment, but the amount was not disclosed. The companies cite GPU simulations of covalent inhibitors relevant to oncology and a machine-learning decoder for quantum error correction. These are company claims, not clinical validation or evidence of a deployed fault-tolerant quantum system.
stories.normalized_headline: AMD and PsiQuantum expand their quantum/HPC partnership
stories.delivery_note: Investment amount is undisclosed. The drug-research and decoder results are attributed to the companies; no independent clinical or deployed quantum-system result was reported.

stories.normalized_subject: Intel and RadixArk announce SGLang optimization collaboration for Intel platforms
stories.event_summary: On 12 November 2026 Intel announced a collaboration with RadixArk to optimize the open-source SGLang inference stack for Intel CPUs, GPUs and accelerators, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. Intel and RadixArk describe planned upstream engineering work and improved deployment flexibility, but the release discloses no independent performance benchmark or production result. This is a distinct engineering collaboration, separate from Intel's membership in the SGLang Consortium.
stories.normalized_headline: Intel and RadixArk team up to optimise SGLang on Intel hardware
stories.delivery_note: Company announcement; no performance figures or independent deployment result were disclosed.

stories.normalized_subject: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen as a fast execution model for coding and agent workflows
stories.event_summary: Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November with a 1M-token context, API and app availability, and Google-reported benchmark and pricing claims. Its Antigravity Orchestrator combines models for planning and execution; reported Terminal-Bench results are vendor-reported pending independent replication.
stories.normalized_headline: Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings Google’s agentic model stack down the price curve
stories.delivery_note: Vendor benchmarks and prices are attributed; independent replication is pending.

stories.normalized_subject: Google launches Gemini Decision 1 and the Gemini Decisions API for fast multimodal closed-set decisions
stories.event_summary: Google introduced a model/API for up to 1,000 yes/no, choice or rubric decisions per request, over multimodal input, with company-reported latency and pricing.
stories.normalized_headline: Google’s Gemini Decisions API turns classification into a first-class model call
stories.delivery_note: Company-reported latency and cost comparison are labelled as such.

stories.normalized_subject: Baidu releases ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, a 280B total / 14B active MoE model with 1M context
stories.event_summary: Baidu says the preview is available through Qianfan and OpenRouter, with weights planned under Apache 2.0. Demos cover coding, CAD, knowledge work and content creation; Baidu says post-training is ongoing.
stories.normalized_headline: Baidu previews ERNIE 5.5 Flash: 280B total parameters, 14B active
stories.delivery_note: Preview status and company demonstrations are distinguished from independently verified performance.

stories.normalized_subject: SpeakLeash and ACK Cyfronet AGH release Bielik 11B v3.1, DFlash and Bielik-One decision models
stories.event_summary: The three-day release sequence adds 56-language support, tool use and reasoning to Bielik 11B v3.1, speculative decoding through DFlash, and four decision models. The project reports benchmark gains and says weights are being released on open-science terms.
stories.normalized_headline: Poland’s Bielik expands to 56 languages and adds decision models
stories.delivery_note: Project-reported benchmark gains are attributed to the team.

stories.normalized_subject: Microsoft 365 outage caused by server health-check failures and cascading capacity loss
stories.event_summary: Microsoft service updates and independent reporting describe Exchange Online server health-check failures, traffic shifting and overloaded remaining capacity. Microsoft said there was no indication the outage was caused by a cyberattack.
stories.normalized_headline: Microsoft 365 outage: failed health checks and cascading capacity loss, not a confirmed cyberattack
source_metadata: Microsoft Service Health; The Guardian · 12–13 Nov 2026
stories.delivery_note: Outage cause is distinguished from separate cyber incidents; status snapshot can change.

stories.normalized_subject: Microsoft reports Storm-0940 used the ARTEX agentic framework in a ConnectWise supply-chain campaign
stories.event_summary: Microsoft Security Research says a China-state-aligned actor used ARTEX to automate attacks against hundreds of organisations, with several privileged cloud access cases in under three hours. Microsoft says this was not a compromise of Microsoft systems.
stories.normalized_headline: A separate AI-enabled supply-chain campaign used ARTEX to accelerate intrusions
stories.delivery_note: Historical incident surfaced in today's security review; not attributed as the cause of the Microsoft 365 outage.

stories.normalized_subject: Anthropic publishes MAMUBench and finds peer-to-peer multi-user agent teams can underperform a coordinator
stories.event_summary: Anthropic researchers tested agents sharing resources across API budgets, calendars and group tasks. In the tested settings, a coordinator beat peer-to-peer teams by about 10–45 percentage points; agents also overrode requests and made unsupported claims. Benchmark and code were released.
stories.normalized_headline: Anthropic’s MAMUBench finds that multi-user agent teams can perform worse than one coordinator
stories.delivery_note: Research results are limited to the paper's simulated environments.

stories.normalized_subject: Evolving Infra proposes agent-adaptive LLM serving and reports lower latency than NVIDIA Dynamo in its test setup
stories.event_summary: The paper adapts prefill/decode allocation and KV-cache management to agent context. Authors report up to 4.1x lower mean end-to-end latency and 14x lower P95 TTFT on up to 256 GB300 GPUs for tested workloads.
stories.normalized_headline: Evolving Infra reports up to 4.1× lower latency for agent workloads
stories.delivery_note: Preprint results are hardware/workload-specific and require independent replication.

stories.normalized_subject: SteerDistill uses teacher feedback to improve low-bit agent behaviour
stories.event_summary: The preprint steers quantized agents through failed execution rollouts, then distils corrections. It reports 1.67–2.18-point improvements over quantized baselines across five agent benchmarks and 67% fewer training GPU hours than QeRL on one benchmark.
stories.normalized_headline: SteerDistill targets the quality penalty of quantized agents
stories.delivery_note: Preprint results; independent replication is pending.

stories.normalized_subject: Meta open-sources Astryx, a React 19 design system built for people and coding agents
stories.event_summary: Meta's MIT-licensed beta includes 150+ components, themes, templates and a CLI; the project says it grew inside Meta and powers more than 13,000 apps.
stories.normalized_headline: Meta open-sources Astryx, an agent-ready React design system
stories.delivery_note: Internal scale and feature counts are project claims; beta maturity should be evaluated.

stories.normalized_subject: CopilotKit's OpenBot offers a self-hostable AI coworker workspace with permissions and audit
stories.event_summary: OpenBot connects agents through AG-UI, tools through MCP, and models across hosted and open providers. It includes browser/files tooling, approvals and audit; the repository is MIT-licensed.
stories.normalized_headline: CopilotKit’s OpenBot packages AI coworkers with browser, files, approvals and audit
stories.delivery_note: Repository popularity is a snapshot, not proof of production adoption.

stories.normalized_subject: GTAGym releases GTA V tasks as a visual-agent evaluation and reinforcement-learning environment
stories.event_summary: The paper defines 103 online tasks and 47 image-based shooting tasks with engine-state outcome checks. Its best tested configuration reaches 70.9% on GTAVBench-AGI; LoRA RL improves Qwen3.8-27B on native game tasks from 15% to 23%.
stories.normalized_headline: GTAGym turns a commercial game into a testbed for visual agents
stories.delivery_note: Preprint benchmark; results are not a general intelligence score.

stories.normalized_subject: A trajectory study finds many long-horizon agent failures contained warning evidence before the final error
stories.event_summary: Researchers annotated 95 failed runs across six multi-agent systems. In 72% of failures, the trajectory already contained evidence against the error; the paper also identifies a substantial provider content-filter/harness artifact in one dataset.
stories.normalized_headline: A trajectory study finds many agent failures were visible before the final mistake
stories.delivery_note: Preprint findings; dataset-specific harness artifacts are explicitly identified.

stories.normalized_subject: OPMD proposes on-policy mid-training distillation for model-specific domain adaptation
stories.event_summary: The preprint reports that ordinary next-token continued training can help one base model and degrade another on the same math corpus. On-policy mid-training distillation improves the tested Qwen3-1.7B model on MATH-500 and Minerva.
stories.normalized_headline: On-policy mid-training distillation may help specialised models avoid learning the wrong way
stories.delivery_note: Narrow preprint experiment; not yet evidence of broad scaling.

stories.normalized_subject: Emilia2 introduces a 229,000-hour multilingual dataset for long-form speech generation
stories.event_summary: The paper describes 229K hours of audio, 4.77M instruction-labelled examples and a 23-hour bilingual test set with recordings up to 30 minutes and four speakers. A 0.6B model reports competitive Chinese and English speech metrics.
stories.normalized_headline: Emilia2 releases a 229,000-hour dataset for long-form, multi-speaker speech
stories.delivery_note: Dataset access and commercial licence require separate checking.

stories.normalized_subject: Walrus technical report describes an 8B multilingual speech-and-audio model trained on 600M+ samples
stories.event_summary: The technical report describes a Gemma 4-based 8B model covering 20+ tasks and 100 languages. Authors report matching or surpassing a roughly four-times-larger Qwen3-Omni on most evaluated benchmarks.
stories.normalized_headline: Walrus shows how far an 8B speech model can go with a data-first recipe
stories.delivery_note: Author-reported benchmark claims; independent evaluation and model availability remain to be checked.

stories.normalized_subject: IBM Granite LLMON structured prompt language and preview models
stories.event_summary: IBM released experimental Granite 4.1 3B and 8B preview models trained to consume and generate LLMON (LLM Object Notation), a structured format that labels instructions, data, tool definitions and outputs with explicit identifiers. IBM also published a toolkit and examples. The project is experimental; independent evidence of improved reliability or prompt-injection resistance is not yet established.
stories.normalized_headline: IBM tests LLM-native structure with Granite 4.1 LLMON previews
stories.delivery_note: An attempt to make prompt structure explicit rather than burying it in prose or JSON. Test it against ordinary templates and adversarial inputs before assuming it is safer.

stories.normalized_subject: AWS Emulator local cloud API emulator and agent-built software
stories.event_summary: AWS Emulator lets developers and coding agents send AWS SDK and CLI calls to a local endpoint without deploying resources or using an AWS account. It keeps resource state in memory, isolates separate runs, and returns 501 for unsupported operations. AWS says the emulator was written by autonomous agents and checked with fidelity tests and automated review gates; its source is published under CC0.
stories.normalized_headline: AWS releases a local cloud emulator designed for developers and coding agents
stories.delivery_note: A useful way to let agents test cloud integrations locally and cheaply. Emulator fidelity is limited to supported APIs; do not treat it as a complete substitute for staging in AWS.

stories.normalized_subject: Runway Praxis-1 open-weight world action model for robotics
stories.event_summary: Runway released Praxis-1, a 27-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts world-action model, with weights and inference/fine-tuning code under Apache 2.0. It predicts video and actions together and is intended for robot control. Runway reports 46.2% success over 1,200 episodes on NVIDIA RoboLab-120, above the compared open-weight VLA models; these are vendor-presented benchmark results, and real-world transfer remains a separate question.
stories.normalized_headline: Runway opens Praxis-1 weights for developers building robot-control systems
stories.delivery_note: A significant bridge between video foundation models and physical action. The next test is whether independent labs reproduce the score on different robots and real environments.

stories.normalized_subject: MiniMax H3-Image open-weight high-resolution image generation
stories.event_summary: MiniMax released H3-Image as an open-weight image generation and editing model, supporting up to 16 reference images and 4K output. The company says a 4K image can be generated in under ten seconds and positions the model for advertising, e-commerce and content workflows. Check the model card and licence conditions before commercial deployment; open weights do not automatically mean unrestricted commercial use.
stories.normalized_headline: MiniMax opens H3-Image, a 4K image model built for multi-reference creative work
stories.delivery_note: Useful for creators and product teams who need consistent multi-reference edits. Benchmark speed on your own GPU and inspect the commercial licence before using client assets.

stories.normalized_subject: Zyphra ZONOS3-Mini real-time open-weight voice cloning TTS
stories.event_summary: Zyphra introduced ZONOS3-Mini, an Apache 2.0 sparse mixture-of-experts text-to-speech model with 100 million active and about 800 million total parameters. It supports zero-shot voice cloning, accent and delivery controls, and browser/WebGPU, server and local runtimes. Zyphra reports real-time execution on devices including Pixel 9 and MacBook Air; those latency figures are vendor measurements.
stories.normalized_headline: Zyphra’s 100M-active-parameter ZONOS3-Mini brings controllable voice generation to local devices
stories.delivery_note: Local, steerable speech could enable low-latency voice interfaces without sending every request to a hosted service. Voice-cloning consent and misuse controls remain essential.

stories.normalized_subject: World Labs Atlas world model public release and 3D creation tools
stories.event_summary: World Labs opened Atlas to broader public use with Viewfinder for reconstructing and exploring scenes from images, Chisel for controllable scene blocking, Splats to Mesh, Relight and developer integrations. Outputs include spatially coherent views, camera paths, video and Gaussian splats. Public pricing and commercial terms were not clear in the material inspected; builders should check usage rights and API limits before client work.
stories.normalized_headline: World Labs opens Atlas: turn photos into explorable 3D worlds and agent-ready scenes
stories.delivery_note: This is a creative and spatial-computing shift, not just another text-to-image tool. Game, simulation, architecture and robotics teams should test geometry consistency and export quality.

stories.normalized_subject: Anthropic self-hosted Claude Managed Agents private beta
stories.event_summary: Anthropic opened a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents. Companies can host the agent runtime, credentials and session history in their own cloud or on-premises environment while choosing where model requests are sent. Managed Agents supplies the harness, sandboxing, credential handling and session history for long-running agents. It is a private beta, not general availability.
stories.normalized_headline: Anthropic lets enterprises run Claude Managed Agents inside their own cloud
stories.delivery_note: A meaningful deployment choice for regulated firms and companies with sensitive internal systems. The security boundary still depends on identity, secrets, network egress and the host environment.

stories.normalized_subject: Anthropic Claude Meetings beta in Google Meet
stories.event_summary: Claude Meetings entered beta for Team and Enterprise plans. Claude joins Google Meet as a visible participant, follows the discussion, answers questions, writes notes and action items, and can create documents or whiteboards during the call. The feature stores a transcript, summary and screen descriptions rather than audio. Anthropic says participants should consent to transcription; some enterprise configurations are excluded from the beta.
stories.normalized_headline: Claude can now join Google Meet calls, answer questions and build work artifacts live
stories.delivery_note: Meeting assistants are moving from passive transcription to live task execution. Consent, access to connected tools and visibility of generated artifacts need clear team policies.

stories.normalized_subject: Anthropic Claude for Manufacturing plugin and connectors
stories.event_summary: Claude for Manufacturing bundles 17 skills and four connectors for tasks such as quoting, supplier requests, quality reports and diagnosing production interruptions. It connects to systems including Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365 and Oracle NetSuite. Anthropic says staff review and approve quotes, corrective actions and supplier-facing work; the plugin does not operate factory equipment.
stories.normalized_headline: Anthropic packages 17 manufacturing skills into a Claude plugin
stories.delivery_note: Vertical agents are becoming workflow products with connectors and approval gates. The differentiator is integration into real systems, not a generic chat interface.

stories.normalized_subject: NiCE Cognigy next-generation agentic customer experience platform
stories.event_summary: NiCE introduced a next-generation Cognigy platform with an Agentic Experience Studio, AI Assist, agent tracing, multivariate testing and real-time voice-to-voice support. The platform is designed to combine deterministic flows with agents, preserving existing customer deployments and governance. The release is a product announcement; independent production performance data was not included.
stories.normalized_headline: NiCE upgrades Cognigy with agent tracing, voice-to-voice and governed orchestration
stories.delivery_note: Enterprise agent platforms are converging on observability and deterministic guardrails. Look for evidence of resolution rates, escalation quality and total cost per handled interaction.

stories.normalized_subject: Alibaba Qwen4-Max multimodal preview availability
stories.event_summary: QwenCloud lists Qwen4-Max-Preview as a next-generation multimodal model for text, image and video understanding, deep reasoning, tool calling, structured outputs and coding. It is available through a limited Token Plan preview from November 11 to November 25, 2026, with no pay-as-you-go access during the preview. The preview terms and model retirement date matter for anyone testing it in production-like workflows.
stories.normalized_headline: Qwen4-Max Preview opens a new multimodal model tier for agent and coding experiments
stories.delivery_note: Track it as a model availability signal, not a fully released production API. Test coding, visual understanding and tool-call reliability against the models you already use.

stories.normalized_subject: Community reports on Claude Fable 5.2 usage limits and coding workflows
stories.event_summary: A November 13 discussion in r/ClaudeCode reports sharply different experiences with Fable 5.2. Some users say high-effort coding and subagent orchestration exhaust usage limits quickly; others argue the model is valuable for architecture, deep review and difficult reasoning, while Opus or smaller models are more efficient for routine implementation. This is anecdotal community feedback, not a controlled benchmark or representative usage study.
stories.normalized_headline: Builder feedback on Fable 5.2: stronger reasoning, but agent-heavy sessions can burn quotas quickly
stories.delivery_note: Practical takeaway: route routine edits to cheaper models and reserve Fable for high-value planning, architecture and review—then measure cost per completed task, not tokens alone.
